OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The unupgraded branch registers an ABSOLUTE cost, not a delta. Enlightenment.cs:21-24 is `SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(1, reduceOnly: true)`, a LocalCostModifier of type Absolute with value 1 (CardEnergyCost.cs:197-203); the port wrote `add_cost_this_turn(1 - card.energy_cost)`, a RELATIVE modifier computed from the cost at that instant, which drifts the moment the card's base cost changes within the same turn. `Card.set_cost_this_turn` is the absolute form and was already there. EXECUTED: a 3-cost Bludgeon reads 1 after Enlightenment and STILL reads 1 after being upgraded to base 2 in the same turn, where the delta form read 0 -- and card/armaments and card/apotheosis both upgrade cards in hand.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  The this-turn/this-combat split between the two branches was already correct and is untouched. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: The BRANCH is right and easy to get backwards, so it is worth stating: unupgraded uses `SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(1, reduceOnly: true)` and UPGRADED uses `SetThisCombat(1, reduceOnly: true)` (Enlightenment.cs:21-28), and the sim maps them to `add_cost_this_turn` and `set_cost_this_combat(1)` respectively (event_cards.py:330-333) -- the this-turn/this-combat split is correct. THE UNUPGRADED BRANCH USES A DELTA WHERE C# USES AN ABSOLUTE SET. C# registers a LocalCostModifier of type Absolute with value 1 (CardEnergyCost.cs:197-203, LocalCostModifier.cs class comment); the sim writes `card.add_cost_this_turn(1 - card.energy_cost)`, a Relative modifier computed from the cost AT THAT INSTANT. The two agree while the card's base cost is unchanged, and diverge the moment it changes within the same turn: a 3-cost card gets delta -2 in the sim, so if it is then UPGRADED mid-turn to base 2 the sim reads 0 while C# still reads its absolute 1. LIVE -- Enlightenment is granted by the ported Zen Weaver event, and card/armaments and card/apotheosis both upgrade cards IN HAND during the same turn, with several Ironclad cards dropping a cost on upgrade (barricade, apotheosis, body_slam, corruption, dark_embrace, ...). The sim already has the right primitive: `Card.set_cost_this_turn` (cards/base.py:252-258) is the absolute form and is used elsewhere.

guards.what: `reduceOnly` is evaluated LAZILY at cost-calculation time, so C# registers the modifier on EVERY hand card including those already at cost 0 or 1; the sim `continue`s past them (Enlightenment.cs:19-29 vs event_cards.py:328-329)
guards.issue: `LocalCostModifier.IsReduceOnly` is documented as "should this modifier only be INCLUDED IN THE COST CALCULATION if it would lower the cost" (LocalCostModifier.cs) -- a per-read test, not a per-write one. So in the game a 0-cost card in hand still carries an inert reduce-only absolute-1 modifier, and if anything RAISES that card's cost above 1 later in the same turn the modifier activates and clamps it back to 1. The sim's `continue` drops the card permanently. DORMANT: no ported effect raises a hand card's cost within a turn -- the sim's only `add_cost_this_turn` callers pass negative deltas -- so the lazy modifier never activates. Live the moment a cost-RAISING effect is ported.

guards.what: the upgraded branch's `set_cost_this_combat(1)` is not reduce-only in the sim, but the `continue` above it already excluded every card at cost 0 or 1 (event_cards.py:328-331)
guards.rationale: So no card is ever RAISED to 1, which is what reduceOnly guarantees in C#. Same outcome for the upgraded branch; the unupgraded branch's divergence is the OnPlay entry's, not this one's.
